speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I can see you've been waking up frightened; are these episodes happening every night or just occasionally? Also, have you noticed any strange movements, sounds, or sensations when these episodes occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has anyone witnessed her behavior during these episodes, such as talking in her sleep, kicking her legs, or having a sudden startle? REQUEST TEST: Sleep_Study to evaluate for parasomnias or sleep apnea.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The symptoms of frequent frightening dreams with recall, distress upon awakening, and subsequent fatigue in an 8-year-old are classic for this condition; the previous suggestion of Pyelonephritis is incorrect as there are no urinary symptoms and the sleep study will likely show normal architecture. No further tests are needed, but we should establish a consistent bedtime routine and consider brief exposure to the dream narrative to reduce fear.
